statement: On main five sound sets are off, so a build made plainly from main has no beam, knock-out, launch, struggle or transformation sound; Orb's build has three of them on only through build switches.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (three flag flips and the gate runs)
risk: A tester build cut from main without the switch list is quieter than the build Orb approved; seen early by reading the build's packed audio data.

statement: No sound exists for a building being damaged or collapsing, bystanders scattering, the gravity well, or any menu action, and the fight has no ambience or music bed in any build.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (new cue rows on existing synths, a menu hook UI must call)
risk: New cues may need sim events that do not exist for buildings or the gravity well; check the event feed first.
orb_question: Is a dry fight (no ambience, no music) acceptable for Alpha? Recommendation: add one quiet ambience bed and the building and menu sounds; leave bystanders and the gravity well for later.

statement: Nothing in the area is proved by ear: Audio's pages say nobody has listened, and Orb's latest word (2026-11-09) is that the crackles sounded bad, with no record of whether that was the fixed build.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (one listening pass by Orb and a saved record)
risk: Outside testers become the first people to hear the game.
orb_question: Will you do one ten-minute listening pass on a desktop build before testers get it? Recommendation: yes.

statement: Sound on the Alpha's platforms (a Windows desktop build, Linux, the Steam Deck) is not evidenced: every proof is the browser build in Chrome, the only audio project setting is web-only, and no CI job runs an audio check.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (one run per platform saving the audio status line, one listen)
risk: A silent or crackling Deck build is found by a tester, not the team.
depends_on: A Linux desktop build and a Deck tester (PERF area).

statement: There is no music: no track has been handed back, the encoder install was not approved, and the pipeline has never run end to end.
risk: First real track exposes loop, loudness or terms problems late.
orb_question: Does Alpha need music? Recommendation: no; ship with a quiet ambience bed and run the music test after Alpha.

statement: Stacked impacts overdrive the engine's limiter (peaks +1.1 to +9.3 dBFS before it, up to 2.3% of samples over its threshold) on the mixer path a desktop build uses, and the resulting distortion was never measured or heard.
risk: Busy fights sound squashed on desktop even with no stall.

statement: The pad-only silent start in the browser is half fixed: the engine-side hook and the start-menu line that warns the player are parked, and the getter built for it is read by nothing.
risk: Affects only private browser looks; the Alpha's platforms are desktop builds.

statement: Legal's ruling on the music tool rests on summaries of its terms read on 2026-10-04, and says so; no re-read is recorded before a track would ship to outside testers.
risk: Terms change again before a track ships; matters only if music is in Alpha.

statement: No audio check runs in CI, and two sound data files (co-op and moments) have no schema rule, so a broken cue file would only warn.
risk: A sound regression lands unnoticed because nobody listens and nothing checks.

statement: Leftovers: the caption babble voice is unreached by the game, a schema rule points at a music file that does not exist, and nine audio parks stay on disk although two are fully on main and one is withdrawn.
risk: Stale parks get re-applied over newer code.

statement: The sound pipeline is wired into the game: the host creates the cue reader and voice pool and warms the sound bank at start, and Orb reported that sound worked on a browser build.
The browser crackle fix is on main and in Orb's build, with saved before-and-after measurements (holes of 66.7 and 106.7 ms gone at 100 and 150 ms stalls).
Settings has Master, Effects and Voice volume and Mono sound.
The music paperwork is ahead of the music: a ruling, a notice file, an origin-log row and an About-page sentence held off by a flag until a track ships.
